items.title: Observer energy, spatial momentum, invariant mass, rest energy and kinetic energy of a four-momentum
items.statement:
Throughout, $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ is the oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski
model of [[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]], $c>0$, and $n\in V$ is future unit
timelike, $\eta(n,n)=-1$ ([[def-lorentz-form-and-inertia]],
[[def-time-orientation-and-future-causal-sets]]). Write
$n^\perp=\{v\in V:\eta(n,v)=0\}$ for the rest space of $n$,
$h(v):=v+\eta(n,v)n$ for the rest
projection and $|w|:=\sqrt{\eta(w,w)}$ for the norm on $n^\perp$
([[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]\,(c)); recall from that
clause that $h$ is linear with image $n^\perp$ and kernel $\mathrm{span}(n)$,
that $V=\mathrm{span}(n)\oplus n^\perp$, and that the restriction of $\eta$ to
$n^\perp$ is positive definite.

**(a) Observer energy, spatial momentum and invariant mass.** For every $P$ in
the future closed cone $\mathrm{cl}(C^+)$ define

$$E_n(P):=-c\,\eta(P,n), \qquad q_n(P):=h(P),$$

and, when $P$ is nonzero future causal, define the **invariant mass** of $P$ by

$$m(P):=\frac{\sqrt{-\eta(P,P)}}{c} .$$

Then $q_n(P)\in n^\perp$, $\eta(n,P)=-E_n(P)/c$, and

$$P=\frac{E_n(P)}{c}\,n+q_n(P)$$

is the unique decomposition of $P$ as a real multiple of $n$ plus a vector of
$n^\perp$: a vector $P$ has $P=\lambda n+w$ with $\lambda\in\mathbb R$ and
$w\in n^\perp$ if and only if $\lambda=E_n(P)/c$ and $w=q_n(P)$. Equivalently,
$E_n(P)$ and $q_n(P)$ are the unique pair consisting of a real number and a
vector of $n^\perp$ with that property. The pair $(E_n,q_n)$ is the
restriction to $\mathrm{cl}(C^+)$ of the pair of linear maps
$P\mapsto -c\,\eta(P,n)$ and $P\mapsto h(P)$ on $V$. For future null $P$ the
formula for $m(P)$ gives $m(P)=0$, because $\eta(P,P)=0$.

**(b) Rest-mass parameter, rest energy and kinetic energy.** Let $m>0$ and let
$P=mU$ with $U$ future timelike and $\eta(U,U)=-c^2$, the four-velocity
normalisation of [[def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration]]. Then call $m$
the **rest-mass parameter** of $P$ as written, $mc^2$ its **rest energy**, and

$$T_n(P):=E_n(P)-mc^2$$

its **kinetic energy** relative to the observer $n$. Bilinearity gives
$\eta(P,P)=m^2\eta(U,U)=-m^2c^2$, so $m=m(P)>0$ is determined by $P$.
Thus $T_n(P)=E_n(P)-m(P)c^2$ is a function of $(P,n)$ on the future
timelike cone; recording $m$ supplies no independent parameter.

**(c) No positivity, inequality or measurement claim.** This definition claims
no positivity of $E_n$, no inequality or vanishing property of $T_n$, and no
physical measurement. The names observer energy, spatial momentum, invariant
mass, rest energy and kinetic energy, and the units joule, kilogram metre per
second and kilogram, belong to the unit conventions of
[[def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions]] and to the physical postulates
of this framework; the mathematical content asserted here is only the explicit
dependence of the five quantities on $P$, $n$ and $m$.

**(d) What the objects depend on.** $E_n$ and $q_n$ are functions of the pair
$(P,n)$: $q_n(P)$ is an element of the vector space $V$, not a coordinate
triple, and no basis of $V$ enters its definition, while
$E_n(P)=-c\,\eta(P,n)$ uses the Lorentz form alone. $m(P)$ depends on the
scalar $\eta(P,P)$ alone and hence on no observer and no basis; $T_n(P)$
uses the rest mass $m=m(P)$ fixed by that scalar. No choice principle is
used.
items.strategy: Definition item fixing five quantities and their exact dependence. Obligations: (i) $h$ is the linear projection of [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]\,(c) with image $n^\perp$ and kernel $\mathrm{span}(n)$, so $q_n(P)\in n^\perp$ and the decomposition $P=-\eta(P,n)n+h(P)$ is unique; (ii) $-\eta(P,P)\ge0$ on $\mathrm{cl}(C^+)$ by [[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]], so the square root defining $m(P)$ is well defined for every nonzero future causal $P$; (iii) no positivity, monotonicity or measurement statement is imported here — those are supplied by [[lem-sr-energy-momentum-observer-identities]] and by [[post-sr-massive-particle-dynamics]]; (iv) $T_n$ is defined only after a rest-mass parameter $m$ is fixed, so it cannot be read as a function of $P$ and $n$ alone. No choice principle is used.

items.title: Positivity, mass shell and kinetic energy of the observer quantities of a four-momentum
items.statement:
Let $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ be the oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski model
([[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]]), $c>0$, let $n\in V$ be future unit
timelike, $\eta(n,n)=-1$, and let $E_n,q_n,m,T_n$ be the quantities of
[[def-sr-observed-energy-momentum-and-kinetic-energy]].

**(a)** If $P$ is nonzero future causal, then $E_n(P)>0$, $q_n(P)\in n^\perp$
and

$$\eta(q_n(P),q_n(P))=\frac{E_n(P)^2}{c^2}+\eta(P,P)\ \ge\ 0 .$$

Consequently: (i) if $P$ is future null, then $\eta(P,P)=0$ and
$E_n(P)=c\,|q_n(P)|>0$; (ii) if $P$ is future timelike with invariant mass
$m(P)$, then $\eta(P,P)=-m(P)^2c^2$ and the mass-shell identity

$$E_n(P)^2=m(P)^2c^4+c^2\,|q_n(P)|^2$$

holds. The invariant mass $m(P)$ depends only on the scalar $\eta(P,P)$ and
therefore on no observer $n$ and no basis, while $E_n$ and $q_n$ do depend on
$n$.

**(b)** Let $P=mU$ with $m>0$ constant, let $U$ be future timelike with
$\eta(U,U)=-c^2$ (the four-velocity normalisation of
[[def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration]]), and put
$\gamma:=-\eta(U/c,n)\ge1$ and $w:=c\,h(U/c)/\gamma\in n^\perp$, the
relative velocity of [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]\,(d)
applied to the future unit vector $u=U/c$; equivalently $w=h(U)/\gamma$. Then

$$E_n(P)=mc^2\gamma,\qquad T_n(P)=mc^2(\gamma-1)\ \ge\ 0,\qquad q_n(P)=m\gamma w,$$

and $m(P)=m$. Moreover $T_n(P)=0$ if and only if $\gamma=1$, that is $U=cn$,
equivalently $P=mcn$ (the particle is at rest relative to $n$). Finally
$|q_n(P)|=m\gamma|w|=mc\sqrt{\gamma^2-1}$.
items.strategy: All clauses are algebra in the flat model. (a) Expand $q_n(P)=P+\eta(P,n)n$: bilinearity and $\eta(n,n)=-1$ give $\eta(q_n,q_n)=\eta(P,P)+\eta(P,n)^2$, and $\eta(P,n)=-E_n(P)/c$. Positivity of $E_n$: choose an $\eta$-orthonormal basis with first vector in $C^+$ ([[lem-lorentz-form-has-orthonormal-basis]], [[lem-future-oriented-inertial-frames-exist]]) and write $P=P^0e_0+P_s$, $n=n^0e_0+n_s$; then $n^0>|n_s|$ and $P^0\ge|P_s|$ by [[lem-timelike-cone-has-two-convex-components]], so $-\eta(P,n)=P^0n^0-P_s\cdot n_s\ge n^0|P_s|-|n_s|\,|P_s|=|P_s|(n^0-|n_s|)\ge0$ using the finite Cauchy-Schwarz inequality ([[thm-cauchy-schwarz-finite]], [[def-spatial-euclidean-structure-of-an-inertial-frame]]); equality forces $P_s=0$, and then $P\ne0$ gives $P^0>0$ and $-\eta(P,n)=P^0n^0>0$. Substitute $\eta(P,P)=-m(P)^2c^2$ for (ii). (b) From $u:=U/c=\gamma(n+w/c)$ of [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]\,(d) one gets $q_n(P)=mc\,h(u)=m\gamma w$ and $E_n(P)=-mc\,\eta(U,n)=mc^2(-\eta(U/c,n))=mc^2\gamma$; the rest is the identity $|w|^2=c^2(1-\gamma^{-2})$ and $\gamma\ge1$ from the same item, with $\gamma=1$ if and only if $u=n$. No choice principle is used.

items.title: Four-momentum components, energy-velocity relation and passive boost transformation in an inertial frame
items.statement:
Let $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ be the oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski model
([[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]]), $c>0$, and let
$(o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ be an inertial frame with stationary observer $n:=e_0$
([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]); let $E_n,q_n$ be the observer
quantities of [[def-sr-observed-energy-momentum-and-kinetic-energy]].

**(a)** For every $P\in\mathrm{cl}(C^+)$ the coordinate components of $P$ in
the frame are $(P^0,P^1,P^2,P^3)=(E_n(P)/c,\,q^1,q^2,q^3)$, where
$q_n(P)=\sum_{i=1}^3q^ie_i$; if $P$ is future timelike then
$E^2=m(P)^2c^4+c^2\sum_{i=1}^3(q^i)^2$ with $E=E_n(P)$.

**(b)** Let $x:I\to A$ be a $C^1$ future timelike worldline
([[def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline]]) whose chart coordinate path is
$t\mapsto(ct,r(t))$, with coordinate velocity $w:=r'$ and
$\gamma_w:=(1-|w|^2/c^2)^{-1/2}$
([[def-spatial-euclidean-structure-of-an-inertial-frame]],
[[def-rational-power]]); then $|w|<c$, the four-velocity is
$U=\gamma_w(c,w)$ by [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]\,(e),
and for $P=mU$ with $m>0$ constant the components are $P=m\gamma_w(c,w)$, that
is $E_n(P)=m\gamma_wc^2$ and $q_n(P)=\sum_{i=1}^3m\gamma_ww^ie_i$.

**(c)** Let $B(\beta)$ be the passive boost of [[def-lorentz-boost]] with
parameter $\beta=(v/c)s$, where $v\in\mathbb R$, $|v|<c$, and
$s\in\mathbb R^3$ is a unit spatial coordinate vector ($s\cdot s=1$), and let $P'$
denote the components of the same vector $P$ after the coordinate change
$x'=B(\beta)x$, with $B(\beta)$ here denoting its frame matrix. Put
$\gamma_v:=(1-v^2/c^2)^{-1/2}$, $\mathbf p:=(P^1,P^2,P^3)$,
$p_\parallel:=s\cdot\mathbf p$, $\mathbf p_\parallel:=p_\parallel s$ and
$\mathbf p_\perp:=\mathbf p-p_\parallel s$, with the same projections
defining the primed components. Then

$$P'^0=\gamma_v\bigl(P^0-(v/c)\,p_\parallel\bigr),\qquad \mathbf p'_\parallel=\gamma_v\bigl(\mathbf p_\parallel-(v/c)P^0s\bigr),\qquad \mathbf p'_\perp=\mathbf p_\perp,$$

equivalently $E'=\gamma_v(E-v\,p_\parallel)$,
$p'_\parallel=\gamma_v(p_\parallel-vE/c^2)$, $\mathbf p'_\perp=\mathbf p_\perp$. The quadratic
combination is invariant,
$E'^2-c^2|\mathbf p'|^2=E^2-c^2|\mathbf p|^2=m(P)^2c^4$ for future timelike
$P$, while for future null $P$ one has $E=c|\mathbf p|$ and
$E'=c|\mathbf p'|$ in both coordinate systems; in particular the invariant
mass is frame-independent.
items.strategy: Read observer decomposition in the frame basis; apply the passive boost matrix with unit direction s and vector parameter beta=(v/c)s. Define gamma_v=(1-v²/c²)^(-1/2), scalar p_parallel=s dot p and vector p_parallel s; use v/c as the scalar coefficient. Treat v=0 with B(0)=I. Expand the Lorentz quadratic form and preserve future null positivity.

items.title: Proper-time derivative of a vector field along a worldline and the four-force notation
items.statement:
Let $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ be the affine Minkowski model, $c>0$, and let $x:I\to A$ be a $C^1$ future timelike worldline with proper-time function $\tau:I\to J$ and inverse $\rho:J\to I$ ([[def-sr-proper-time]], [[lem-sr-proper-time-parametrization]]).
(a) For a $C^1$ map $P:I\to V$ define its proper-time derivative $\dot P:I\to V$ by
$$\dot P(s):=\frac{P'(s)}{\tau'(s)},$$
where $P'$ is the derivative of $P$ with respect to the worldline parameter, taken componentwise in any affine basis of $V$; the result does not depend on the basis because two affine bases differ by a constant invertible linear map. Equivalently $\dot P(s)=(P\circ\rho)'(\tau(s))$, so $\dot P$ is the derivative of the proper-time parametrised field $P\circ\rho$. Since $\tau'(s)>0$ by [[lem-sr-proper-time-parametrization]], $\dot P$ is well defined and continuous whenever $P$ is $C^1$.
(b) If $P=mU$ with $m>0$ constant and $U$ the four-velocity of $x$ ([[def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration]]), then $F:=\dot P$ is called the four-force on the particle; in an inertial frame $F$ has the components of the derivative of the four-momentum with respect to proper time.
(c) This item introduces a derivative and a name only. It asserts no force law, no field equation, no equation of motion and no existence or uniqueness of solutions; the identities satisfied by $F$ for a stipulated four-momentum field are proved in [[lem-sr-four-force-and-work-energy-identities]], and a physical force law requires a further model premise.
items.strategy: Definition item. Obligations: (i) the division by $\tau'$ is legitimate because $\tau'>0$ ([[lem-sr-proper-time-parametrization]]); (ii) the equivalence $\dot P(s)=(P\circ\rho)'(\tau(s))$ is the chain rule along the reparametrisation, $\rho$ being the inverse of the increasing function $\tau$; (iii) componentwise differentiation in one affine basis and change of basis commute because the transition map is constant and linear, so the definition is basis-free; (iv) no dynamics is imported: $F$ is a derived vector field attached to a given $P$, not a prescribed law. No choice principle is used.

items.title: Four-force identities and the work-energy relation in an inertial frame
items.statement:
Let $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ be the oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski model
([[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]]), $c>0$, and let
$(o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ be an inertial frame with $n:=e_0$
([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]). Let $x$ be a $C^2$ future
timelike worldline whose chart coordinate path is $t\mapsto(ct,r(t))$, with
coordinate velocity $w:=r'$, coordinate acceleration $a:=w'$ and
$\gamma:=(1-|w|^2/c^2)^{-1/2}$
([[def-spatial-euclidean-structure-of-an-inertial-frame]]); let $m>0$ be
constant, $P:=mU$ with $U=\gamma(c,w)$ the four-velocity
([[def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration]],
[[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]\,(e)), $E:=E_n(P)$,
$\mathbf p:=m\gamma w:I\to\mathbb R^3$, so that
$q_n(P)=\sum_{i=1}^3p^ie_i$, $F:=\dot P$ the four-force
of [[def-sr-proper-time-derivative-and-four-force]] and
$\mathbf f:=\frac{d}{dt}\mathbf p$ the coordinate three-force.

**(a)** $F=mA$, where $A$ is the four-acceleration, and $\eta(P,F)=0$;
equivalently $\eta(U,F)=0$ and the mass shell $\eta(P,P)=-m^2c^2$ has
vanishing proper-time derivative.

**(b)** $\frac{dE}{dt}=\mathbf f\cdot\mathbf w$, the Euclidean inner product
of the coordinate vectors.

**(c)** $F=\gamma\,(\mathbf f\cdot\mathbf w/c,\ \mathbf f)$, that is
$F^0=\gamma\,\mathbf f\cdot\mathbf w/c$ and $F^i=\gamma\mathbf f^i$ for
$i=1,2,3$.

**(d)** If instead $m:I\to(0,\infty)$ is $C^1$ and $P=mU$ with this variable
parameter, define $F:=\dot P$ by the general derivative clause (a) of
[[def-sr-proper-time-derivative-and-four-force]]. Then
$\eta(P,F)=-mc^2\,\frac{dm}{d\tau}$, the derivative being taken
with respect to the proper-time parameter.
items.strategy: Direct computation in the frame. With $E=m\gamma c^2$ and $\gamma'=\gamma^3(w\cdot a)/c^2$ ([[thm-real-power-continuity-and-derivatives]], [[thm-chain-rule]]) one has $dE/dt=m\gamma^3(w\cdot a)$; together with $\mathbf p=m\gamma w$ and $\mathbf f=m(\gamma^3(w\cdot a)w/c^2+\gamma a)$ this gives $\mathbf f\cdot\mathbf w=m\gamma^3(w\cdot a)=dE/dt$, proving (b). Since $\dot P=\gamma\,dP/dt$ and $dP/dt=(mc\gamma',m\gamma'w+m\gamma a)$, substituting gives (c). For (a), $\dot P=m\dot U=mA$ because $m$ is constant, and $\eta(U,A)=0$ by [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]\,(b); equivalently differentiate $\eta(P,P)=-m^2c^2$ along the worldline. For (d), differentiate $\eta(P,P)=-m(\tau)^2c^2$: $2\eta(P,F)=-2mc^2\,\frac{dm}{d\tau}$. No force law is used; the identities are conditional on the stated four-momentum field. No choice principle is used.

items.title: Total four-momentum, invariant mass and center-of-momentum frame of a finite system
items.statement:
Throughout, $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ is the oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski
model of [[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]] and $c>0$.

**(a) Total four-momentum.** For a finite list $(P_1,\dots,P_N)$, $N\ge0$, of
vectors of $V$, define the **total four-momentum**
$P_{\mathrm{tot}}:=\sum_{i=1}^{N}P_i$ as the finite sum of
[[def-finite-sum-in-a-commutative-monoid]] in the additive group $(V,+)$ of
the vector space $V$; the empty sum is $0$. The sum uses the vectors $P_i$
alone: no event, no position and no simultaneity datum enters it, and the
order of the list does not affect $P_{\mathrm{tot}}$ because addition in $V$
is commutative.

**(b) Invariant mass of the total.** If $P_{\mathrm{tot}}$ is future timelike
([[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]],
[[def-time-orientation-and-future-causal-sets]]), define the **invariant
mass** of the system and its **rest energy** by

$$M:=M(P_{\mathrm{tot}}):=\frac{\sqrt{-\eta(P_{\mathrm{tot}},P_{\mathrm{tot}})}}{c}>0$$

and its rest energy is $Mc^2$.

The square root is a real number because
$\eta(P_{\mathrm{tot}},P_{\mathrm{tot}})<0$ for a timelike vector, and it is
strictly positive, so $M>0$ ([[def-rational-power]]). If
$P_{\mathrm{tot}}$ is future null, set $M:=0$ and say that the system has no
rest frame. For $P_{\mathrm{tot}}$ equal to zero, spacelike or past causal,
this convention defines no invariant mass.

**(c) Center-of-momentum frame.** A **center-of-momentum frame** of a nonzero
$P_{\mathrm{tot}}$ is an inertial frame $(o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$
([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]) whose first vector satisfies

$$h_{e_0}(P_{\mathrm{tot}})=0,\qquad h_{e_0}(v):=v+\eta(v,e_0)e_0\quad(v\in V),$$

where the projection is defined on all of $V$; for a future causal total this
is $q_{e_0}(P_{\mathrm{tot}})=0$, meaning that its total spatial momentum
vanishes for the observer stationary in the frame
([[def-sr-observed-energy-momentum-and-kinetic-energy]]). The condition is equivalent to
$P_{\mathrm{tot}}=-\eta(P_{\mathrm{tot}},e_0)e_0$, i.e. to
$P_{\mathrm{tot}}\in\mathrm{span}(e_0)$; if $P_{\mathrm{tot}}$ is future
timelike this holds exactly when $P_{\mathrm{tot}}=\lambda e_0$ with
$\lambda>0$, and then $E_{e_0}(P_{\mathrm{tot}})=Mc^2$ for $M$ as in (b).

**(d) Comparison with the single-vector convention.** For a single future
timelike vector $P$, the invariant mass $M$ of (b) coincides with $m(P)$ of
[[def-sr-observed-energy-momentum-and-kinetic-energy]]; in particular if
$P=mU$ with $m>0$ and $\eta(U,U)=-c^2$ (the four-velocity normalisation of
[[def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration]]), then $M=m$. Both quantities
are functions of the scalar $\eta(P,P)$ alone.

**(e) Scope.** This definition asserts no existence of a center-of-momentum
frame (that is [[lem-sr-center-of-momentum-frame]]), no physical conservation
law and no dynamics; only the total vector carries the invariant mass, and the
individual summands need not be causal for the sum to be defined. No choice
principle is used.
items.strategy: Definition item. Obligations: (i) the finite sum is the one of [[def-finite-sum-in-a-commutative-monoid]] in the abelian group $(V,+)$; (ii) $-\eta(P_{\mathrm{tot}},P_{\mathrm{tot}})>0$ for future timelike $P_{\mathrm{tot}}$ by [[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]], so the square root is well defined; (iii) the equivalence in (c) is immediate from $q_{e_0}(P)=h(P)=P+\eta(P,e_0)e_0$; (iv) no frame is produced here — existence is [[lem-sr-center-of-momentum-frame]], so the definition is not circular; (v) clause (d) compares the two invariant-mass conventions, both functions of the scalar $\eta(P,P)$. No choice principle is used.

items.title: Finite sums of future causal vectors and additivity of observer energy and momentum
items.statement:
Let $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ be the oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski model
([[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]]) and $c>0$.

**(a)** If $v,w\in\mathrm{cl}(C^+)$, then $v+w\in\mathrm{cl}(C^+)$; if in
addition $v\in C^+$ or $w\in C^+$, then $v+w\in C^+$. Moreover
$-\eta(v,w)\ge0$ for $v,w\in\mathrm{cl}(C^+)$, with equality if and only if
$v=0$, or $w=0$, or both $v$ and $w$ are nonzero future null and
$w=\lambda v$ for some $\lambda>0$.

**(b)** If $P_1,\dots,P_N$ with $N\ge1$ are nonzero future causal vectors,
then $P_{\mathrm{tot}}=\sum_{i=1}^{N}P_i$
([[def-sr-total-four-momentum-and-invariant-mass]]\,(a)) is a nonzero future
causal vector; if at least one $P_i$ is future timelike, then
$P_{\mathrm{tot}}$ is future timelike. The converse implication does not
hold: two future null vectors that are not parallel have a future timelike
sum.

**(c)** For every future unit $n$ ([[def-lorentz-form-and-inertia]]) and all
$P_1,\dots,P_N\in\mathrm{cl}(C^+)$,

$$E_n\Bigl(\sum_{i=1}^{N}P_i\Bigr)=\sum_{i=1}^{N}E_n(P_i),\qquad q_n\Bigl(\sum_{i=1}^{N}P_i\Bigr)=\sum_{i=1}^{N}q_n(P_i),$$

where $E_n,q_n$ are the observer quantities of
[[def-sr-observed-energy-momentum-and-kinetic-energy]]; if the $P_i$ are
nonzero future causal, then $E_n(P_{\mathrm{tot}})>0$.
items.strategy: Work in an $\eta$-orthonormal basis whose first vector lies in $C^+$ ([[lem-lorentz-form-has-orthonormal-basis]], [[lem-future-oriented-inertial-frames-exist]]), so that $\mathrm{cl}(C^+)=\{v:v^0\ge|v_s|\}$ and $C^+=\{v:v^0>|v_s|\}$ by [[lem-timelike-cone-has-two-convex-components]]. For (a), $(v+w)^0=v^0+w^0\ge|v_s|+|w_s|\ge|v_s+w_s|$ by the triangle inequality, with strict first inequality if one summand is timelike; $-\eta(v,w)=v^0w^0-v_s\cdot w_s\ge|v_s||w_s|-v_s\cdot w_s\ge0$ by Cauchy-Schwarz ([[thm-cauchy-schwarz-finite]]), and equality forces $v_s,w_s$ collinear with $v^0=|v_s|$, $w^0=|w_s|$ unless a vector vanishes, i.e. both are null and parallel. For (b), apply (a) repeatedly by induction on $N$ ([[thm-induction-principle]], [[def-finite-sum-in-a-commutative-monoid]]); nonzeroness follows from $\mathrm{cl}(C^+)\cap(-\mathrm{cl}(C^+))=\{0\}$ of [[def-time-orientation-and-future-causal-sets]]: if $P_{\mathrm{tot}}=0$ then $P_N=-\sum_{i<N}P_i$ lies in $\mathrm{cl}(C^+)$ and in $-\mathrm{cl}(C^+)$, hence is zero, contradicting the hypothesis. For the failure of the converse, in an orthonormal basis take $P_1=(1,1,0,0)$ and $P_2=(1,0,1,0)$ times a common positive energy over $c$: both are future null and not parallel, and their sum $(2,1,1,0)$ times that factor has $v^0=2>\sqrt2=|v_s|$, hence is future timelike. For (c), $\eta(\cdot,n)$ and $h$ are linear ([[def-sr-observed-energy-momentum-and-kinetic-energy]], [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]\,(c), [[def-linear-map]]); positivity is [[lem-sr-energy-momentum-observer-identities]]\,(a) applied to the nonzero future causal total of (b). No choice principle is used.

items.title: Center-of-momentum frames of a future timelike four-momentum and their unique time vector
items.statement:
Let $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ be the oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski model
([[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]]), $c>0$, and let $Q\in V$ be future
timelike with invariant mass $M:=\sqrt{-\eta(Q,Q)}/c$
([[def-sr-total-four-momentum-and-invariant-mass]]\,(b)); put
$n_Q:=Q/(Mc)$, so that $\eta(n_Q,n_Q)=-1$, $n_Q\in C^+$ and $Q=Mc\,n_Q$.

**(a)** There exists an inertial frame $(o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ with $e_0=n_Q$;
in every such frame $q_{e_0}(Q)=0$, $E_{e_0}(Q)=Mc^2$ and the components of
$Q$ are $(Mc,0,0,0)$. Such a frame is a center-of-momentum frame of $Q$ in the
sense of [[def-sr-total-four-momentum-and-invariant-mass]]\,(c).

**(b)** Conversely, if an inertial frame satisfies $q_{e_0}(Q)=0$, then
$e_0=n_Q$. Hence the time vector of a center-of-momentum frame of $Q$ is
unique, and two center-of-momentum frames of $Q$ differ only by the choice of
origin and by a positively oriented $\eta$-orthonormal change of the spatial
basis $(e_1,e_2,e_3)$ of $n_Q^\perp$; in particular the center-of-momentum
frame at a fixed origin is unique up to spatial rotations.

**(c)** If $Q$ is a nonzero future null vector, then no inertial frame
satisfies $q_{e_0}(Q)=0$: a nonzero future null vector has no
center-of-momentum frame.
items.strategy: Normalize future timelike Q to n_Q=Q/(Mc), choose a finite orthonormal basis of n_Q-perp, correct its orientation by one sign and choose any event as origin. The converse forces e0=n_Q only; frames retain arbitrary origin and spatial-rotation freedom. A nonzero null Q cannot lie on a unit timelike axis.

items.title: Collision data and four-momentum conservation
items.statement:
Throughout, $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ is the oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski
model of [[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]] and $c>0$.

**(a) Collision datum and conservation.** A **collision datum** is a triple
$(p;(P_1,\dots,P_N);(P'_1,\dots,P'_K))$ consisting of an event $p\in A$, a
finite nonempty list $(P_1,\dots,P_N)$, $N\ge1$, of vectors of $V$, called the
incoming legs, and a finite nonempty list $(P'_1,\dots,P'_K)$, $K\ge1$, of
vectors of $V$, called the outgoing legs. Its **side totals** are the finite
sums of [[def-finite-sum-in-a-commutative-monoid]] in the additive group
$(V,+)$, formed as in [[def-sr-total-four-momentum-and-invariant-mass]]:

$$Q_{\mathrm{in}}:=\sum_{i=1}^{N}P_i,\qquad Q_{\mathrm{out}}:=\sum_{j=1}^{K}P'_j .$$

The datum **conserves** when $Q_{\mathrm{in}}=Q_{\mathrm{out}}$. The two sides
are compared only through these totals: if two data have the same incoming
legs and the same outgoing legs, their conservation behaviour is the same, and
for a datum with a single leg on each side conservation is exactly
$P_1=P'_1$.

**(b) Legs, mass data and mass sums.** A leg $P$ is **massive with mass**
$m>0$ if there is a future timelike $U\in V$ with $\eta(U,U)=-c^2$ (the
four-velocity normalisation of [[def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration]])
and $P=mU$; a leg is **null** if it is a nonzero future null vector
([[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]],
[[def-time-orientation-and-future-causal-sets]]). For a massive leg both $U$
and $m$ are determined by $P$: $\eta(P,P)=-m^2c^2$ forces
$m=\sqrt{-\eta(P,P)}/c$, the invariant mass $m(P)$ of
[[def-sr-observed-energy-momentum-and-kinetic-energy]], and then $U=P/m$; so
the recorded mass of a massive leg is necessarily its invariant mass. A datum
is **on-shell** if every leg is massive or null; a **mass-specified** datum is
an on-shell datum together with the recorded mass $m>0$ of each massive leg
and the recorded value $0$ for each null leg. The **mass sum** of a side of a
mass-specified datum is the sum of the recorded positive masses of its
massive legs, and the side is **massive-only** if all its legs are massive.

**(c) Special classes of data.** A datum is **causal** if every leg lies in
$\mathrm{cl}(C^+)$; **two-leg** if $N=K=2$; and **equal-mass** if, in addition
to being two-leg, the recorded masses agree pair by pair, that is the
incoming masses $(m_1,m_2)$ equal the outgoing masses $(m'_1,m'_2)$ under the
identification of the pairing.

**(d) Scope.** The definition is purely mathematical: it neither asserts that
any datum describes a physical process, nor that a conserving datum exists for
a prescribed list of legs, nor any law of nature. Position, simultaneity,
mechanism and interaction strength are not part of a datum; only the event,
the two finite lists and their recorded masses are. In particular
conservation here is an equation between two vectors of $V$ and is not the
adopted conservation law of a physical model, which is a separate postulate;
the existence question for prescribed masses is answered only in special
cases by [[lem-sr-collision-necessary-conditions]]. No choice principle is
used.
items.strategy: Definition item. Obligations: (i) the side totals use the finite sums of [[def-finite-sum-in-a-commutative-monoid]] in the additive group $V$; (ii) the massive-leg clause uses the four-velocity normalisation of [[def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration]] and the null-leg clause the causal classification of [[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]]; (iii) no physical content is smuggled in: conservation is an equation between two vectors, and the existence of a conserving datum with prescribed masses is a separate mathematical question answered only in special cases by [[lem-sr-collision-necessary-conditions]]; (iv) the definition is not the adopted conservation law of the physical model, which is a postulate of its own. No choice principle is used.

items.title: Invariant mass, center-of-momentum frame and necessary conditions for conserving collision data
items.statement:
Let $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ be the oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski model
([[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]]), $c>0$, and let
$\mathcal D=(p;(P_1,\dots,P_N);(P'_1,\dots,P'_K))$ be a mass-specified
conserving collision datum of [[def-sr-collision-datum-and-conservation]],
causal and on-shell, all of whose legs are nonzero; write
$Q:=Q_{\mathrm{in}}=Q_{\mathrm{out}}$ for the common side total.

**(a)** If $Q$ is future timelike with invariant mass $M$, then $M$ is the
common invariant mass of both sides, $Q$ has the center-of-momentum frame of
[[lem-sr-center-of-momentum-frame]] with $e_0=Q/(Mc)$, and in that frame

$$Mc^2=\sum_{\text{legs of a side}}E_{e_0}(\text{leg})\qquad\text{for each side};$$

each massive leg $\ell=mU$ has $E_{e_0}(\ell)=mc^2\gamma_\ell\ge mc^2$ with
$\gamma_\ell:=-\eta(U/c,e_0)$ and equality if and only if $U=ce_0$, and each
null leg has $E_{e_0}>0$. Hence for each side
$S\in\{\mathrm{in},\mathrm{out}\}$,

$$M\ \ge\ \sum_{\text{massive legs }\ell\in S}m_\ell,$$

with equality if and only if $S$ is massive-only and every massive leg of $S$
has four-velocity $ce_0$ (all massive particles of that side at rest in the
center-of-momentum frame).

**(b)** If $Q$ is future null, then every leg is null, all legs are mutually
parallel in one future null direction, $M=0$ by the convention of
[[def-sr-total-four-momentum-and-invariant-mass]]\,(b), and no
center-of-momentum frame exists.

**(c)** Suppose the incoming side is two-leg, $P_i=m_iU_i$ with $m_i>0$, and
put $n_2:=U_2/c$ (the future unit observer comoving with the second leg),
$\gamma:=-\eta(U_1/c,n_2)\ge1$ and $E:=E_{n_2}(P_1)=m_1c^2\gamma$. Then

$$M^2=m_1^2+m_2^2+\frac{2m_2E}{c^2}.$$

Consequently, if the outgoing side is mass-specified with massive masses
$\mu_1,\dots,\mu_L$, $L\ge1$ (it may also contain null legs), the datum can
conserve only if

$$E\ \ge\ \frac{c^2}{2m_2}\Bigl[\Bigl(\sum_{l=1}^L\mu_l\Bigr)^2-m_1^2-m_2^2\Bigr],\qquad\text{equivalently}\qquad T:=E-m_1c^2\ \ge\ \frac{c^2}{2m_2}\Bigl[\Bigl(\sum_{l=1}^L\mu_l\Bigr)^2-(m_1+m_2)^2\Bigr].$$

**(d)** Suppose the incoming side consists of exactly two future null legs
$P_1,P_2$. If there is an inertial frame with
$P_i=(E_i/c)(e_0+s_i)$, $E_i>0$, $s_1,s_2$ unit spatial vectors with
$s_2=-s_1$, then $Q$ is future timelike and $M=2\sqrt{E_1E_2}/c^2$. More
generally, with $s_1,s_2$ unit spatial vectors in that frame and
$\sigma:=s_1\cdot s_2\in[-1,1]$ ([[thm-cauchy-schwarz-finite]]), if
$\theta:=\arccos\sigma\in[0,\pi]$ is their **Euclidean angle**, with
$\arccos:[-1,1]\to[0,\pi]$ the inverse of the continuous strictly decreasing
restriction of cosine in [[def-principal-inverse-sine-and-cosine]]. Here
$\cos x=\sum_{j=0}^\infty(-1)^jx^{2j}/(2j)!$ is the function of
[[def-sine-and-cosine-by-power-series]], and $\pi$ is twice its smallest
positive zero ([[def-pi-via-first-positive-cosine-zero]]). Thus
$\cos\theta=\sigma$, $\theta=0\iff\sigma=1$, and
$\theta=\pi\iff\sigma=-1$. Then
$Q$ is future timelike for $\theta\ne0$ with

$$M=\frac{\sqrt{2E_1E_2(1-\cos\theta)}}{c^2},$$

while for $\theta=0$ the total $Q$ is future null, $M=0$ and no
center-of-momentum frame exists. In particular, a conserving on-shell
collision datum whose incoming side is a single null leg and whose outgoing
side contains at least one massive leg does not exist.

**(e)** All clauses are conditional implications from the hypotheses of a
conserving, causal, on-shell datum. They assert no interaction, no existence
of a conservation process for prescribed legs, no cross section, amplitude or
probability, and no empirical fact.
items.strategy: Assemble the local suppliers. By [[lem-sr-finite-future-causal-sums]] each side total is a nonzero future causal vector; if some leg is timelike the total is timelike, and observer energy and momentum are additive with $E_{e_0}(Q)>0$. (a) For timelike $Q$, [[lem-sr-center-of-momentum-frame]] supplies the frame $e_0=Q/(Mc)$ with $E_{e_0}(Q)=Mc^2$; additivity gives $Mc^2=\sum E_{e_0}$ on each side; [[lem-sr-energy-momentum-observer-identities]]\,(b) gives $E_{e_0}(\ell)=mc^2\gamma_\ell\ge mc^2$ with equality exactly for $U=ce_0$, and clause (a)(i) gives $E_{e_0}(\ell)=c|q|>0$ for null legs; summing yields the inequality and its equality case. (b) If one leg were timelike, the total would be timelike; and for future causal $v,w$ one has $-\eta(v,w)\ge0$ with equality exactly for zero or parallel future null pairs by [[lem-sr-finite-future-causal-sums]]\,(a), so a null total forces every pair of nonzero legs to be parallel future null; [[lem-sr-center-of-momentum-frame]]\,(c) excludes a center-of-momentum frame. (c) From $P_2=m_2c\,n_2$ and $\eta(P_1,n_2)=-E/c$ one gets $\eta(P_1,P_2)=-m_2E$ and $\eta(P_2,P_2)=-m_2^2c^2$, $\eta(P_1,P_1)=-m_1^2c^2$, so $-\eta(Q,Q)=m_1^2c^2+m_2^2c^2+2m_2E$; divide by $c^2$. The threshold inequality applies (a) to the outgoing side, $\sum_l\mu_l\le M$, and rearranges. (d) In the displayed frame $\eta(P_1,P_2)=(E_1E_2/c^2)(-1+\cos\theta)$, so $-\eta(Q,Q)=2E_1E_2(1-\cos\theta)/c^2$, and for $\theta=0$ the total is a positive multiple of the null vector $P_1$; the one-null-leg statement follows because a sum containing a timelike leg is timelike while a single null leg leaves $Q$ null. No choice principle is used; all arguments are finite-dimensional and algebraic.

items.title: Adopted massive-particle momentum, observer measurement and isolated-collision conservation
items.statement:
Adopt as physical assumptions of the relativistic particle model, on top of the
flat spacetime model of [[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]] and the SI unit
conventions of [[def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions]], together with
the framework's idealisations of point particles, ideal clocks and ideal light
signals:

**(i) Mass and momentum.** Every massive classical particle of the model
carries a positive constant invariant mass parameter $m>0$ and has
four-momentum $P=mU$, where $U$ is the four-velocity of its future timelike
worldline ([[def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline]],
[[def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration]],
[[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]); $P$ is a vector of $V$
whose SI unit is kilogram metre per second. The formula is adopted only for
$m>0$; the case $m=0$ is not defined by it and is the separate premise
[[post-sr-ideal-massless-particle-momentum]]. In particular $\eta(P,P)=-m^2c^2$
is a consequence of the four-velocity normalisation, not a separate
assumption.

**(ii) Observer measurement identification.** Relative to a future unit
observer $n$, the model identifies the measured energy of the particle with
$E_n(P)$, its measured spatial momentum with $q_n(P)$, its kinetic energy with
$T_n(P)=E_n(P)-mc^2$ and its rest energy with $mc^2$, where $E_n,q_n,T_n$ are
the quantities of [[def-sr-observed-energy-momentum-and-kinetic-energy]]; the
units are the joule, kilogram metre per second and kilogram of
[[def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions]]. This clause is a formulation
convention identifying mathematical quantities with the quantities the model
calls measured; it is not a measurement report and no experiment is claimed.

**(iii) Isolated collision balance.** An isolated collision is represented by
a mass-specified on-shell collision datum at an event, with finite nonempty
incoming and outgoing lists of the massive particles of (i) and/or the ideal
massless particles of [[post-sr-ideal-massless-particle-momentum]], and with
no external four-momentum transfer or omitted leg. The interaction is
idealized as confined to that event. The sum of the incoming four-momenta equals the sum of the
outgoing four-momenta, in the sense of the collision data of
[[def-sr-collision-datum-and-conservation]]: the model adopts
$Q_{\mathrm{in}}=Q_{\mathrm{out}}$ for such an isolated datum. No particular
collision is asserted to occur, and no mechanism, probability, cross section
or amplitude is supplied by this clause.

**(iv) Equation of motion for a stipulated force.** Put
$H_c^+:=\{U\in C^+:\eta(U,U)=-c^2\}$. A stipulated force law is a given
map $F:D\to V$ on a given subset $D\subseteq A\times H_c^+$,
with force components in $\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm m/\mathrm s^2$. No regularity
away from the specified worldline is assumed. Along a given $C^2$ massive worldline
$x:I\to A$ with $(x(s),U(s))\in D$ for all $s\in I$, the model's particle
equation is $m\,dU/d\tau=F(x,U)$, with
$dU/d\tau$ the proper-time derivative of
[[def-sr-proper-time-derivative-and-four-force]], so that the stipulated $F$
is the four-force of the motion. A particular force law, and the existence,
uniqueness and domain of solutions of the resulting equation, are not adopted
here and belong to a separate model.

Empirical support for these assumptions is a nonlogical relation of the
framework, not a proof; the idealisations of point particles, ideal clocks,
ideal light signals and flat spacetime are inherited and travel to every
consumer of this premise.
items.strategy: Postulate: an adopted physical premise, not a theorem. Obligations: (i) $P=mU$ uses the four-velocity of [[def-sr-four-velocity-and-acceleration]] with its normalisation $\eta(U,U)=-c^2$ of [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]; (ii) the measurement identification names the mathematical quantities $E_n,q_n,T_n$ of [[def-sr-observed-energy-momentum-and-kinetic-energy]] and the SI units of [[def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions]] and explicitly disclaims observation; (iii) conservation is stated for an isolated collision only, as an equality of the side totals of [[def-sr-collision-datum-and-conservation]], with no existence or mechanism claim; (iv) the equation of motion form is adopted only for a stipulated force, and no force law is adopted. Empirical support for the assumptions is a nonlogical relation of the framework, not a proof; the idealisations of point particles, ideal clocks and flat spacetime are inherited and must travel to consumers.
items.physical_scope: Classical massive point particles with positive constant invariant mass in flat Minkowski spacetime, with ideal clocks, ideal light signals and SI conventions. The model identifies E_n, q_n, T_n with observer measurements and adopts four-momentum balance for isolated collisions, including ideal massless legs as defined by the separate massless postulate. The single-particle equation applies only to massive C2 worldlines. Excludes internal structure, spin, radiation reaction, variable-mass dynamics, gravity, continuum matter, quantum and statistical effects, and empirical reports; a force law and interaction mechanism are separate premises.

items.title: Adopted momentum model for an ideal massless particle
items.statement:
Adopt as a separate model premise for ideal massless particles, independent of
[[post-sr-massive-particle-dynamics]] whose formula $P=mU$ uses $m>0$ and does
not define a massless case:

**(i) The object.** An ideal massless particle of the model is described by a
nonzero future null vector $P\in V$
([[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]],
[[def-time-orientation-and-future-causal-sets]]) whose SI unit is kilogram
metre per second ([[def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions]]). Such a $P$
is not of the form $mU$ for any $m>0$ and any future timelike $U$ with
$\eta(U,U)=-c^2$: a positive multiple of a timelike vector is timelike, and
the zero vector is neither timelike, null nor spacelike, so the massive
expression $mU$ with this normalized $U$ degenerates
to $0$ at $m=0$ and does not describe a nonzero null momentum. The particle
therefore has no four-velocity, no proper-time parametrisation and no rest
frame. Its scale is fixed by a measured energy in an observer's frame.

**(ii) Observer identification.** Relative to a future unit observer $n$, the
model identifies the measured energy and spatial momentum of the particle with
the quantities $E_n(P)=-c\,\eta(P,n)$ and $q_n(P)=h(P)$ of
[[def-sr-observed-energy-momentum-and-kinetic-energy]]. Necessarily
$E_n(P)=c\,|q_n(P)|>0$, by
[[lem-sr-energy-momentum-observer-identities]]\,(a)(i), and no rest mass, rest
energy or kinetic energy is assigned to the particle — the definition of
$T_n$ requires a rest-mass parameter $m$ and no such parameter is introduced
here. This clause is a formulation convention identifying mathematical
quantities with the quantities the model calls measured; it is not a
measurement report and no experiment is claimed.

**(iii) No identification with light or quantum objects.** The ideal massless
particle is not identified here with light, with a classical wave or with any
quantum object: no frequency, wavelength, quantisation, polarisation or
Planck constant enters this premise, and the identification of light with
massless particles requires the wave model and its own postulates on a
separate page.

**(iv) No process.** This premise asserts no interaction of massless
particles and no decay or production process; such processes require a
stipulated dynamics. Empirical support for the assumption is a nonlogical
relation of the framework, not a proof, and the idealisations inherited from
the flat spacetime model and the ideal-point description travel to every
consumer of this premise.
items.strategy: Postulate for the massless case, kept separate because $P=mU$ at $m=0$ degenerates to $0$ ([[def-sr-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]]: the zero vector is neither timelike, null nor spacelike) and cannot describe a nonzero null momentum. Obligations: (i) the object is a nonzero future null vector, using the causal classification and time orientation; (ii) the identification of $E_n$ and $q_n$ is a formulation convention, with the mathematical identity $E_n=c|q_n|$ supplied separately by [[lem-sr-energy-momentum-observer-identities]] and not adopted; (iii) no identification with light or with quantum concepts is made; (iv) no process is asserted. Empirical support is a nonlogical relation, not a proof.
items.physical_scope: Ideal classical massless point particles in flat Minkowski spacetime, modelled by a nonzero future null four-momentum whose energy and momentum are identified with the observer quantities, and whose scale is fixed by a measured energy. Excludes four-velocities, proper time and rest frames for the particle, any massive limit m -> 0, the identification with light or classical waves, quantum properties, and every interaction, decay, production or empirical claim.

items.title: Energy, momentum, invariant mass and four-force of relativistic particles, and necessary collision thresholds
items.statement:
Adopt [[post-sr-massive-particle-dynamics]] and
[[post-sr-ideal-massless-particle-momentum]]. Then the following conditional
physical claims hold in the flat classical model, with the units of
[[def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions]].

**(a) Massive particle.** Let a massive particle have constant mass $m>0$,
four-momentum $P=mU$ and a future unit observer $n$. Its measured energy
$E_n(P)=-c\,\eta(P,n)$, spatial momentum $q_n(P)=h(P)$ and kinetic energy
$T_n(P)=E_n(P)-mc^2$ satisfy $E_n(P)>0$, $T_n(P)\ge0$ and the mass-shell
identity $E_n(P)^2=m^2c^4+c^2|q_n(P)|^2$; $T_n(P)=0$ if and only if the
particle is at rest in the observer's frame ($U=cn$). In an inertial frame
whose stationary observer is $n=e_0$, the components are $P=(E/c,\mathbf p)$
with $E=E_{e_0}(P)=m\gamma_wc^2$ and $\mathbf p=m\gamma_w\mathbf w\in\mathbb R^3$
the coordinates of $q_{e_0}(P)=\sum_{i=1}^3p^ie_i$
for the coordinate velocity $\mathbf w$, and under a passive boost the
components transform as the components of the vector $P$; the combination
$E^2-c^2|\mathbf p|^2=m^2c^4$ is frame-independent.

**(b) Four-force.** Along a $C^2$ worldline with four-acceleration $A$, the
four-force $F=\dot P$ satisfies $\eta(P,F)=0$ and $F=mA$; in an inertial frame
$F=\gamma\,(\mathbf f\cdot\mathbf w/c,\ \mathbf f)$ and
$dE/dt=\mathbf f\cdot\mathbf w$, where $\mathbf f=d\mathbf p/dt$ is the
coordinate three-force. The constancy of $m$ is used; if instead $m$ is a
$C^1$ function $m:I\to(0,\infty)$ along the same worldline, define $P:=mU$
and $F:=\dot P$ by the general derivative construction. As a mathematical identity, $\eta(P,F)=-mc^2\,dm/d\tau$, and the
constant-mass identities are not transferred to variable-mass systems.

**(c) System mass.** For a finite nonempty system of particles all of whose
four-momenta are nonzero future causal, let $Q:=\sum_iP_i$. If $Q$ is
future timelike, its invariant mass $M=\sqrt{-\eta(Q,Q)}/c$ satisfies: in the
center-of-momentum frame with $e_0=Q/(Mc)$ one has
$Mc^2=\sum_iE_{e_0}(P_i)$; every massive constituent has
$E_{e_0}(P_i)\ge m_ic^2$, with equality exactly when it is at rest in that
frame, and every massless constituent has $E_{e_0}(P_i)>0$. Hence
$M\ge\sum_im_i$ over the massive constituents, with equality if and only if
the system is massive-only and all its constituents are at rest in the
center-of-momentum frame. If $Q$ is future null, then $M=0$, all constituents
are massless with parallel momenta, and no center-of-momentum frame exists.

**(d) Massless particle.** An ideal massless particle has
$E_n(P)=c\,|q_n(P)|>0$, has no rest frame and is not $mU$ for any $m>0$; it is
not obtained from the massive formula by setting $m=0$.

**(e) Necessary collision thresholds.** Suppose that, under the adopted
isolated-collision balance, an isolated collision occurs whose incoming legs
are massive particles of constant masses $m_1,\dots,m_N$ and whose outgoing
legs are massive particles of masses $\mu_1,\dots,\mu_K$ and possibly ideal
massless particles. Let $M$ be the invariant mass of the common total
four-momentum $Q$. Then the necessary inequalities $M\ge\sum_im_i$ and
$M\ge\sum_j\mu_j$ hold; if the incoming side is a projectile of mass $m_1$
and a target of mass $m_2$ at rest in the observer frame of the target, with
projectile energy $E$ and kinetic energy $T=E-m_1c^2$ in that frame, then

$$E\ \ge\ \frac{c^2}{2m_2}\Bigl[\Bigl(\sum_{j=1}^K\mu_j\Bigr)^2-m_1^2-m_2^2\Bigr],\qquad T\ \ge\ \frac{c^2}{2m_2}\Bigl[\Bigl(\sum_{j=1}^K\mu_j\Bigr)^2-(m_1+m_2)^2\Bigr],$$

Separately, under the same adopted balance, a single incoming massless particle
cannot produce an outgoing state containing a massive particle. These are kinematic necessity statements under
the adopted conservation: they do not assert that any collision occurs, do
not fix probabilities, amplitudes or cross sections, and are not empirical
findings.

**(f) Scope.** All clauses are conditional on the two postulates and on the
stated idealisations; the conclusions carry the same idealisations. No
measurement, precision, statistical or empirical claim is made.
items.strategy: Conditional deduction assembling the page's suppliers, in this order. (a) The measurement identification is the postulate clause (ii); the identities are [[lem-sr-energy-momentum-observer-identities]]\,(b) and [[lem-sr-four-momentum-in-inertial-frame]]\,(a)-(c), with the frame-independence of $m$ from [[lem-sr-energy-momentum-observer-identities]]\,(a)(ii). (b) [[lem-sr-four-force-and-work-energy-identities]]. (c) [[lem-sr-finite-future-causal-sums]] gives the character of $Q$ and additivity, [[lem-sr-center-of-momentum-frame]] the frame and $E_{e_0}(Q)=Mc^2$, and [[lem-sr-collision-necessary-conditions]]\,(a)-(b) the constituent inequalities and the null case. (d) [[post-sr-ideal-massless-particle-momentum]] with [[lem-sr-energy-momentum-observer-identities]]\,(a)(i) and the degenerate $m=0$ computation. (e) The postulate clause (iii) makes the collision data a conserving collision datum; [[lem-sr-collision-necessary-conditions]]\,(a),(c),(d) gives exactly the displayed necessary inequalities and the one-null-leg impossibility, with the target's rest observer $n_2=U_2/c$ of clause (c). No step asserts existence of an interaction, and no empirical premise is used, so no empirical qualification is carried. Units are those of the model conventions. No choice principle is used.
items.physical_scope: Massive particles with constant positive mass and ideal massless particles described by future null four-momenta in flat Minkowski spacetime with ideal clocks and SI conventions; measured energy, momentum and kinetic energy are the model quantities E_n, q_n, T_n; isolated collisions obey the adopted four-momentum balance at one event, and the stated thresholds are necessary kinematic conditions only. The variable-mass clause is a mathematical derivative identity, not an adopted variable-mass dynamics. Excludes internal structure, spin, radiation reaction, force laws and interaction mechanisms (a separate premise), continuum matter, gravity, quantum and statistical descriptions, and every empirical claim, measurement value or precision statement.

items.title: Four-momentum and kinetic energy at speed three-fifths c
items.statement:
Let $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ be the oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski model
([[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]]), $c>0$, $m>0$, and let
$(o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ be an inertial frame
([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]) in which a massive particle has
four-velocity $U=\gamma_w(c,w)$
([[def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration]],
[[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]\,(e)) with
$w=(3c/5,0,0)$, so that $\gamma_w=5/4$. Then its four-momentum is $P=mU$ with
components $(5mc/4,\,3mc/4,\,0,\,0)$. Relative to the stationary observer
$n=e_0$: $E_n(P)=5mc^2/4$, $q_n(P)$ has coordinates $(3mc/4,0,0)$, the
kinetic energy is $T_n(P)=mc^2/4$, and the mass shell
$E_n(P)^2-c^2|q_n(P)|^2=m^2c^4$ reads
$25m^2c^4/16-9m^2c^4/16=m^2c^4$. The exact kinetic energy
$mc^2/4=0.25\,mc^2$ exceeds the Newtonian expression
$\tfrac12m|w|^2=9mc^2/50=0.18\,mc^2$; the comparison is a numerical
specialisation, not a limiting claim and not a measurement.
items.strategy: Verify each display by exact arithmetic in the frame: $\gamma_w=(1-9/25)^{-1/2}=5/4$; multiply the components of $U$ by $m$; apply [[lem-sr-four-momentum-in-inertial-frame]] and [[lem-sr-energy-momentum-observer-identities]]; compare with the Newtonian value only as a numerical specialisation, not as a limiting claim. No physical measurement is asserted.

items.title: A passive boost that brings a moving particle to rest
items.statement: In the setting of [[ex-sr-four-momentum-at-beta-three-fifths]], let $B(\beta)$ be the passive boost of [[def-lorentz-boost]] with parameter $\beta=3/5$ along $e_1$, and let $P'$ be the components of $P$ after the coordinate change $x'=B(\beta)x$ with $v=3c/5$. Then $P'=(mc,0,0,0)$: the energy becomes $E'=mc^2$ and the spatial momentum vanishes, and the mass shell gives $E'^2-c^2|\mathbf p'|^2=m^2c^4$. The observer energy of the same particle thus changes from $5mc^2/4$ to $mc^2$ while the invariant mass stays $m$; in particular $T_{e'_0}(P)=0$ in the new frame, the frame of the particle's rest.
items.strategy: Substitute $\gamma_v=5/4$, $E=5mc^2/4$, $p_\parallel=3mc/4$ into the boost transformation of [[lem-sr-four-momentum-in-inertial-frame]]\,(c): $E'=\gamma_v(E-vp_\parallel)=5/4\,(5mc^2/4-9mc^2/20)=mc^2$ and $p'_\parallel=\gamma_v(p_\parallel-vE/c^2)=0$. Check the mass shell and read the rest-frame property from [[lem-sr-energy-momentum-observer-identities]]\,(b).

items.title: Two equal masses in head-on motion: system mass exceeds the sum of the masses
items.statement: Let $m>0$ and let two massive particles at a common event have four-momenta $P_1=m\gamma(c,w)$ and $P_2=m\gamma(c,-w)$ with $w=(3c/5,0,0)$ and $\gamma=5/4$. Their total is $Q=P_1+P_2=(5mc/2,0,0,0)$, which is future timelike with invariant mass $M=5m/2$. Since the first basis vector $e_0$ already equals $Q/(Mc)$, the frame is a center-of-momentum frame; moreover $M=5m/2>2m=m_1+m_2$, and the mass excess $(M-2m)c^2=mc^2/2$ equals the total kinetic energy of the two particles relative to $e_0$ ($mc^2/4$ each). Thus the rest mass of the system is not the sum of the rest masses of its parts.
items.strategy: Add the four-momenta in the common frame; identify $Q$ with its first component only, so $-c^2\eta(Q,Q)=c^2(5mc/2)^2$ gives $M=5m/2$ by [[def-sr-total-four-momentum-and-invariant-mass]]; apply [[lem-sr-center-of-momentum-frame]] and [[lem-sr-energy-momentum-observer-identities]]\,(b) for the kinetic energies. The computation is exact at $\gamma=5/4$ and asserts no collision.

items.title: A conserving two-into-one collision datum and the non-uniqueness of its final state
items.statement: In the setting of [[ex-sr-equal-mass-head-on-collision-mass]], the datum with incoming sides $(P_1,P_2)$ and the single outgoing vector $Q=(5mc/2,0,0,0)=(5m/2)c\,e_0$ is an on-shell conserving collision datum: $Q$ is massive with mass $5m/2$ and four-velocity $ce_0$, and $P_1+P_2=Q$. The outgoing rest mass $5m/2$ exceeds the incoming sum $2m$ by $m/2$, and the incoming total kinetic energy $mc^2/2=(M-2m)c^2$ has become rest energy. The final state is not unique: the same total $Q$ is also the sum of two outgoing massive legs at rest with masses $m$ and $3m/2$ (four-velocities $ce_0$), so four-momentum conservation fixes only the total, not the number or masses of the outgoing particles.
items.strategy: Check that the outgoing leg satisfies the massive-leg clause of [[def-sr-collision-datum-and-conservation]] with mass $5m/2$ (its four-velocity is $\eta$-normalised), verify conservation by adding components, and verify the alternative decomposition. Apply [[lem-sr-collision-necessary-conditions]]\,(a) for the mass inequality. The datum is a mathematical configuration; no interaction is asserted.

items.title: Collective mass of a pair of oppositely directed massless momenta
items.statement:
Let $e_0,e_1$ be the first two vectors of an inertial frame, $E_1,E_2>0$, and
let $P_1=(E_1/c)(e_0+e_1)$, $P_2=(E_2/c)(e_0-e_1)$. Both are nonzero future
null vectors with $E_{e_0}(P_i)=E_i$, and their total is
$Q=((E_1+E_2)/c)e_0+((E_1-E_2)/c)e_1$, a future timelike vector with
invariant mass $M=2\sqrt{E_1E_2}/c^2$; for $E_1=E_2=E$ this gives
$Q=(2E/c)e_0$ and $M=2E/c^2$. If instead $P_2=(E_2/E_1)P_1$ (parallel
momenta), then $Q$ is future null, $M=0$ by convention and there is no
center-of-momentum frame. In the opposite-direction case with $E_1\ne E_2$
the first basis vector is not the center-of-momentum vector; the
center-of-momentum frame exists by [[lem-sr-center-of-momentum-frame]] but
differs from the displayed frame. The arithmetic is exact and no measurement
is asserted.
items.strategy: Verify nullness, observer energies and the sum componentwise; compute $-c^2\eta(Q,Q)=(E_1+E_2)^2-(E_1-E_2)^2=4E_1E_2$ and apply [[def-sr-total-four-momentum-and-invariant-mass]]; the parallel case is the null-total clause of [[lem-sr-collision-necessary-conditions]]\,(d). Exact arithmetic, no measurement.

Crowell, Special Relativity, revision 2020-12-10 (author-published undergraduate textbook, 246 PDF pages); signature (+---) converted to (-+++) and c = 1 formulas converted to x^0 = c t; Section 4.3.2 p. 90 Example 7 (two light waves with momenta (E,E) and (E,-E) have total momentum (2E,0) and collective mass 2E)

items.title: Threshold energy for a projectile on a stationary target
items.statement:
Let $m>0$, $\mu>0$ and consider a conserving causal on-shell collision datum whose incoming side is two massive legs, a projectile of mass $m$ with energy $E$ measured by the rest observer $n_2$ of the target, and a target of mass $m$ at rest in that observer's frame, and whose outgoing side is massive with masses $m$, $m$ and $\mu$. By [[lem-sr-collision-necessary-conditions]]\,(c) with $m_1=m_2=m$, $\sum_l\mu_l=2m+\mu$,
$$E\ \ge\ \frac{c^2}{2m}\bigl[(2m+\mu)^2-2m^2\bigr]=mc^2+2\mu c^2+\frac{\mu^2c^2}{2m},$$
equivalently $T=E-mc^2\ \ge\ 2\mu c^2+\dfrac{\mu^2c^2}{2m}$. For $\mu=m$ this reads $E\ge7mc^2/2$ and $T\ge5mc^2/2$. These are necessary kinematic thresholds; the datum need not exist for any concrete interaction.
items.strategy: Substitute into the threshold inequality of [[lem-sr-collision-necessary-conditions]]\,(c) and expand: $[(2m+\mu)^2-m^2-m^2]/(2m)=(2m^2+4m\mu+\mu^2)/(2m)=m+2\mu+\mu^2/(2m)$. Exact algebra; the result is a necessary condition, not a claim that the process occurs.

items.title: A massless four-momentum is not obtained from the massive formula at m = 0
items.statement: Statement refuted: "The four-momentum of an ideal massless particle is obtained by setting $m=0$ in $P=mU$, where $U$ is a future timelike four-velocity with $\eta(U,U)=-c^2$." Refutation. For every future timelike $U$ one has $0\cdot U=0$, and $0$ is not a nonzero future null vector: it is not null (null means $\eta(P,P)=0$ with $P\ne0$) and it has zero energy relative to every observer, $E_n(0)=0$. Conversely, a nonzero future null vector such as $P=(E/c)(e_0+e_1)$, $E>0$, in the first two vectors of an inertial frame satisfies $\eta(P,P)=0$, $E_{e_0}(P)=E>0$, but is not of the form $mU$ with $m>0$ (such a vector is future timelike) or $m=0$ (which gives $0\ne P$). Hence no value of $m\ge0$ produces $P$ by the formula $mU$: a massless momentum is a separate model primitive, and the degenerate case $m=0$ of the massive formula carries no information about it.
items.strategy: Compute directly: $\eta(0,0)=0$ with $0$ excluded from the null class by [[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]]; $\eta(P,P)=(E/c)^2(\eta(e_0,e_0)+\eta(e_1,e_1))=0$ for the displayed $P$; separate the cases $m=0$ and $m>0$ in $P=mU$ and use $\eta(mU,mU)=-m^2c^2<0$ for $m>0$ and timelike $U$. No physical measurement; the positive energy is the observer quantity of [[def-sr-observed-energy-momentum-and-kinetic-energy]].

S. M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1 (1997), Chapter 1; PDF page = printed page + 7; printed p. 27 (the four-velocity is defined only for timelike trajectories; null paths give extra problems)

items.title: Kinetic energy depends on the observer even though the invariant mass does not
items.statement: Statement refuted: "The kinetic energy $T_n(P)=E_n(P)-mc^2$ of a massive particle is a property of the particle alone, independent of the observer $n$." Refutation. With $m>0$, $w=(3c/5,0,0)$, $U=\gamma(c,w)$, $\gamma=5/4$ and $P=mU$ in a frame with $n_1=e_0$, one has $T_{n_1}(P)=mc^2/4\ne0$ by [[ex-sr-four-momentum-at-beta-three-fifths]]; for the observer comoving with the particle, $n_2:=U/c$, one has $U=cn_2$, so $T_{n_2}(P)=0$ by [[lem-sr-energy-momentum-observer-identities]]\,(b). The two future unit vectors $n_1\ne n_2$ are legitimate observers of the same particle and the same vector $P$, so $T_n$ depends on $n$; likewise $E_n$ takes the values $5mc^2/4$ and $mc^2$ while the invariant mass $m$ and the identity $\eta(P,P)=-m^2c^2$ are observer-independent.
items.strategy: Use the two explicit observers from [[ex-sr-four-momentum-at-beta-three-fifths]] and [[ex-sr-four-momentum-boost-to-rest]]: in the particle's rest frame $U=ce'_0$ hence $\gamma=1$ and $T=0$; in the original frame $T=mc^2/4$. Check that both $n_1,n_2$ are future unit. Exact arithmetic; no measurement claim.
